titles: One drop takes the pH from 4.3 to 9.7 | Titration explained
Why a titration flips in a single drop
The sharpest moment in chemistry: the end point
youtube.description:
One drop of base turns a colourless flask pink, and the pH jumps from 4.30 to 9.70. Here is why a titration's end point is so sharp.

What you are seeing: 25.00 mL of 0.100 M hydrochloric acid titrated with 0.100 M sodium hydroxide, with phenolphthalein as the indicator. The curve in the video is the calculated curve, drawn as the base is added.

Method: complete dissociation, ideal solution at 25 °C, volumes additive, one drop taken as 0.05 mL. The pH comes from the charge balance [H+] - Kw/[H+] = (CaVa - CbVb)/(Va + Vb), solved exactly. Activities are taken equal to concentrations, so a real titration differs slightly.

Sources: phenolphthalein colour-change range (pH 8.2 to 10.0) and the ion product of water from the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics.
